answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the primary contract expires in 14 days. memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing and cut unit cost without narrowing service scope, which directly serves the cost-reduction mandate. memory_c1 supports that renewing with the incumbent kept integration stable with no migration risk, which protects the 94%-capacity assembly line that has no buffer. Switching vendors or adding a second source carries onboarding and integration risk the line cannot absorb right now. Negotiating terms is appealing but the contract expires in 14 days; the safest single action that locks in cost savings while eliminating the single-point-of-failure exposure is to renew with the incumbent under multi-year volume terms. This satisfies both the cost mandate and the no-increased-delivery-risk constraint.
